page: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-amd is a High Performance family virtual server utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 12 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage along with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across most multi-threaded and system operations, though single-core metrics show some limitations. The server achieved a Passmark CPU score of 17,153.85 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 27,275.02, both falling in the average range. However, single-core performance is weaker, with a Geekbench single-core score of 947.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 2,219.48. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 1,019.76 GB/sec, which drops to 79.14 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and compression tasks show mixed results; the Passmark CPU encryption test scored 10,762.4, while single-threaded gzip compression was poor at 18.92 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server represents a resource-dense configuration suitable for multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. It performs adequately in static web serving at 7.88 GB/sec and database operations, executing 11.99 million Redis SET operations per second. It is also capable of handling light software compilation and low-parameter LLM inference, processing 131.15 tokens per second for text generation on a small 135M model. However, it is less suited for single-threaded tasks, heavy text processing, or large-scale LLM inference due to its shared CPU architecture and weaker single-core benchmark results.
